entities.name: Anula of Anuradhapura
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Queen Anula of Anuradhapura (r. c. 47–42 BCE) is recorded in the Mahavamsa as the first queen regnant in Sri Lankan history, ruling Rajarata after a sequence of poisoned consorts that chronicles cast as uniquely ruthless. Rising from consort of King Chora Naga, she allegedly disposed of successive husbands before governing in her own name.

Whether read as misogynistic chronicle exaggeration or evidence of palace faction, her five-year reign marks a rupture in Anuradhapura’s male royal sequence. She was finally overthrown and killed, and later kings restored patriarchal succession narratives.

Anula remains a charged symbol of female sovereignty—and its vilification—in early Sri Lankan historiography.
